top.title: Reacts poll: Throw it to Bryant more
top.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Wide receiver Pat Bryant (13) of the Denver Broncos pulls in a catch while cornerback Taron Johnson (3) of the Las Vegas Raiders bears down on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images While Steelers fans are still figuring out WTF just happened with their team in the last five days, Broncos fans are wondering when Pat Bryant is going to become the primary target for Bo Nix. Well, that may be an exaggeration, but Broncos Country does believe No. 13 is the most reliable receiver on a team with a slew of pass-catchers. And the choice wasn’t even close. By a huge margin, Broncos fans think Bryant is one of the best targets for Nix. And by the numbers, they’re not wrong. With just 21 targets, Bryant has caught 16 this season for a total of 221 yards and 2TDs, for a 13.8 average on yards per catch. By comparison, Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton each have more total catches and yards, but the number of drops is much higher. Waddle is 33 of 58 for 398 yards and 2 TDs (12.8 ypc average) and Sutton is 25 of 48 for 266 yards and 2 TDs (10.6 ypc). No wonder only 15% of fans picked Sutton as most reliable and just 1% said Waddle, the receiver who is supposed to be our new super star. Not surprisingly, when Nix is throwing to Bryant his passer rating is gooooooooood . This is wild: Bo Nix has a 146 passer rating when targeting Pat Bryant this year. pic.twitter.com/MoEfU7ATsA — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 26, 2026 While the Broncos have a lot of receiving targets — and all want the ball — second-year Bryant has earned a few more targets than the rest.

top.title: Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones Sends Brian Schottenheimer Message After Eagles Loss
top.description: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a 39-38 defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving . It was their second loss in the last three games despite leading by 21 points. Team owner Jerry Jones send a message about Brian Schottenheimer during his postgame interview. He was promoted to head coach on Jan. 24, 2025, after previously serving as the team’s offensive coordinator. Schottenheimer guided the franchise to a 7-9-1 record in his first year in charge and missed the playoffs for the second straight season. Dallas dropped to 5-7 this campaign and remain in third place in the NFC East. The Eagles are trailing them by half-a-game, while the New York Giants continue to led the division with a 6-3 record. Oct 8, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones speaks to the media before the game at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Jerry Jones opens up on potentially replacing Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer Jerry Jones made it clear that his team doesn’t plan on making a coaching change soon. He added that the focus should be on the upcoming games. “The game where it was ours to take and we didn’t,” Jones said. “So when you look at every whatever, then you have to question everything… You’ve got to look at everything. And that’s certainly not the thought on my mind at this particular time. We’ve got several more games to go and we’ve got to have our mind on that.” Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says that “nothing we saw out there tonight” gives him confidence in Brian Schottenheimer, but he reiterates that a change is not on his mind right now. https://t.co/BipwLyTsE9 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 27, 2026 The 84-year-old added that Dallas has a bigger chance of winning with Brian Schottenheimer in charge. “No, I wouldn’t anticipate that,” Jones said . At this juncture, we can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games, and be where competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes at this time.” The Cowboys have 11 days before they play their next game on Dec. 7. They will visit the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, at Lumen Field in a high-stakes matchup. ABC will broadcast the “Monday Night Football” game live at 8:15 p.m. ET. top.title: Freiburg in ecstasy as remarkable winning streak extends to six matches
top.description: Freiburg in ecstasy as remarkable winning streak extends to six matches SC Freiburg head coach Julian Schuster has praised his squad’s extraordinary team spirit following Thursday evening’s dramatic 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente. The Breisgauer secured their sixth consecutive competitive victory thanks to a stoppage-time winner from Niklas Beste, with Schuster emphasizing the importance of a united dressing room in navigating a demanding schedule. The Freiburg trainer made six changes to the starting XI that defeated Elversberg 1-0 in the Bundesliga last weekend. Cyriaque Irié rewarded Schuster’s faith by scoring the opener in the 11th minute, but Twente remained the more threatening side for much of the first half and eventually equalized through a Younes Taha free kick in the 62nd. Freiburg nevertheless found another way to win. Substitute Derry Scherhant earned a penalty in the 89th minute, and fellow replacement Beste eventually converted the loose ball after Matthias Ginter’s spot kick struck the post. Schuster explains how Freiburg’s team spirit enables squad rotation Speaking to a group of assembled journalists after the post-match press conference, Schuster drew attention to the collective celebrations following Beste’s dramatic winner. The 41-year-old suggested that the team’s togetherness gives him the confidence to rotate extensively without compromising Freiburg’s competitiveness. “That scene in which the team celebrated together is emblematic of this group,” Schuster told the journalists. “That lends us the strength to rotate the squad with full confidence. One sees this with various clubs that have to deal with extreme pressure during this phase [of the season]. There’s also players who have international obligations. The pressure is extreme. “One really can’t leave anyone out,” Schuster continued. “We have this depth and there’s always little things that leave one needing to switch it up. Then it’s nice when players are ready to serve on a regular basis and not to get caught up in the competition of who makes the team sheet. That’s extremely important and I’m very pleased with the lads who started today and were able to make a contribution to the win.” Schuster’s observations build on his earlier comments concerning Freiburg’s exceptional dressing-room culture . In October, the SC trainer emphasized the importance of protecting the club’s special atmosphere and ensuring that difficult personnel decisions do not undermine the collective. The same philosophy has also been emphasized by Freiburg’s players. Veteran midfielder Maximilian Eggestein recently discussed the importance of sacrificing individual ambitions for the team , while Germany internationals Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant credited Freiburg’s supportive club culture when reflecting on their own development. top.title: Josh Uche’s Homecoming: How the Miami Native Found His Footing Again with the Dolphins
top.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images For Miami Dolphins edge rusher Josh Uche , the 2026 NFL season has been more than just another stop on a winding professional journey—it has been a long-awaited homecoming. Signed to a one-year contract in March after bouncing across three teams in two years, the 28-year-old Miami native has quietly re-emerged as a reliable, every-down contributor for a rebuilding Dolphins defense. Early Promise and Breakout in New England Drafted by the New England Patriots in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of the University of Michigan, Uche quickly earned a reputation as an explosive, twitchy pass-rush specialist. After battling injuries and adjusting to the pro game over his first two seasons, he exploded onto the scene in 2022. Operating alongside Matthew Judon, Uche racked up 11.5 sacks and two forced fumbles in 15 games, looking every bit like a cornerstone defender for New England’s future. Two Years of Uncertainty However, replicating that 2022 magic proved difficult. Following a three-sack 2023 campaign, Uche re-signed with New England on a short-term deal before being shipped to the Kansas City Chiefs at the 2024 trade deadline. In Kansas City, Uche struggled to crack Steve Spagnuolo’s defensive rotation, appearing in just six games without recording a sack. Seeking a fresh start in 2025, he signed with the Philadelphia Eagles . While he generated solid pressure rates in limited passing-down snaps, he finished the year with just one sack across 12 appearances, leaving his NFL trajectory at a crossroads entering free agency. Reviving His Career in South Florida When Miami brought Uche home in March 2026, the move flew largely under the radar. Initially viewed as a low-cost depth addition to a revamped linebacker room, Uche has outperformed expectations. Through the first 11 weeks of the 2026 season, Uche has already surpassed his combined sack total from the previous two campaigns: Defensive Production: 38 total tackles, 3.0 sacks, 24 total quarterback pressures, and one forced fumble. Expanded Role: Rather than being pigeonholed strictly as a third-down specialist, Uche has logged over 420 defensive snaps and earned strong marks for his run defense—proving he can hold the edge on early downs as well as collapse the pocket. Looking Ahead For a Dolphins squad navigating roster turnover and key injuries during the 2026 campaign, Uche’s steady play has been a bright spot. Returning to the AFC East—and getting the chance to square off against his former Patriots squad twice a year—has given the South Florida product a renewed edge. As Miami enters the final stretch of the season, Uche is making a compelling case that his best football is still ahead of him right in his own backyard. top.title: Eagles player wasn’t wanted in Dallas. Now he’s getting the last laugh: ‘Packing their bags’
top.description: ARLINGTON, Texas — Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott joked before Thursday’s game that Eagles quarterback Joe Milton was “still a Cowboy” and would help Dallas win. Prescott’s wishes did not come true. Milton crushed the Cowboys and outplayed Prescott, a four-time Pro Bowl quarterback. The Cowboys cut Milton on Aug. 31, and two months later, he left Dallas’ practice squad to join the Eagles’ 53-man roster after Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots. In his third start with Philadelphia, Milton led the Eagles to a 39-38 comeback victory over the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also rushed for a touchdown. “Resilience,” Eagles wide receiver Elijah Moore said of Milton’s performance. “I’m sure that they probably didn’t think the outcome of the game, especially at the end of the game, was going to end up like that. I’m pretty sure that they were probably packing their bags, going inside. And obviously early in the game when it was 31 to 10, they probably thought it was over with. So Joe showed that you never give up. And [if] you continue to sleep [on them], players that you once had are going to come outshine them for another team. And that’s exactly what he showed.” The Eagles looked finished after the Cowboys took a 31-10 lead with 3:40 remaining in the third quarter. But then came Milton. He threw a 45-yard touchdown to DeVonta Smith with 24 seconds left in the third quarter, making it 31-17. He cut Dallas’ lead to eight points (38-30) after rushing for a 15-yard touchdown with 9:17 left in the fourth quarter. On the next drive, he connected with rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon for a 24-yard touchdown to make it a two-point game (38-36) with 2:17 left on the clock. On the Eagles’ last offensive possession, Milton completed two passes to set up Philadelphia’s game-winning field goal. Milton said there was a “lot going through his head” knowing that he was playing against his former team, but he looked unfazed by the moment. Late in the second quarter, the Eagles trailed 21-3 when Milton rolled to his left and threw a 50-yard touchdown to Smith. On that throw, Milton dropped back to the 40-yard line and launched the ball 64.4 yards in the air, the longest touchdown by an Eagles quarterback in the Next Gen Stats era (2016), according to ESPN insights. According to Next Gen Stats, Milton completed 4 of 6 deep passes (20 or more yards) from outside the pocket for 139 yards and three touchdowns, which is the most yards and touchdowns on deep throws in the NGS era. “Heck, yeah, like everybody,” Eagles running back Will Shipley said when asked if he was amazed by Milton’s throws. “Half the time in protection, I’ll look back, the ball will be in the air, and I’m just like, ‘Holy cow.’ I feel like I’m watching it like it’s on TV, but there’s just so much belief in 14 [Joe Milton’s number]. … Everyone in this locker room believes in him as the leader of this team. top.title: Morrison confident Price will 'heal quickly'
top.description: Isaac Price is West Bromwich Albion's top goalscorer in the Championship with seven goals [Getty Images] West Bromwich Albion manager James Morrison is hopeful Isaac Price can return to action ahead of schedule after the midfielder was ruled out for up to six weeks with a knee injury. The 23-year-old came off with an issue in the second half of last Saturday's 2-2 draw at Championship rivals Swansea City . Baggies head coach James Morrison has now confirmed that Price has suffered a grade two medial ligament injury. "He'll be out for roughly six weeks maximum. But, knowing Pricey, he heals quickly," Morrison told BBC Radio WM. "He's a great athlete and a great professional. I'm hoping he'll be a little bit quicker." Coming on top of Mali's Ousmane Diakite being injured on international duty , it leaves Albion light in midfield for Saturday's visit of Bristol City (15:00 GMT) as Rabby Nzingoula misses the game through suspension after being booked in the 3-1 midweek win at Bolton , his fifth yellow card in nine games. "It's something I'll have to speak to him about as three of them could have been avoided," Morrison added. If Price is out for the entire six weeks, he could potentially miss two key encounters with promotion rivals Stoke City, against a meeting with fellow countrymen Ethan Galbraith and Justin Devenny, as well as fixtures against Portsmouth, Cardiff City, Sheffield United, Lincoln City and Preston North End. One option for Saturday is to redeploy left-back Callum Styles, who plays in central midfield for Hungary, but Morrison has also got other options, both short and long term. top.title: Five Good Texans questions with Jacob Barzilla
top.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans takes the field prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images I should start by addressing the first obvious question. Yes, Jacob and I are related. One of the few certain things in life is that when I run into a Barzilla, they have to be a relative. In this case, his grandfather and my father are first cousins. I think that makes me a second cousin once removed or some such technical mumbo jumbo. We will just say we are cousins and leave it at that. So, when I saw his name come across my feed as a Texans analysit I was more than a little curious. If you have downloaded the app, you have seen his analysis posted more than once. It looked like interesting analysis and I am probably a little biased. Everyone knows how talented and brilliant the Barzilla’s are. You can find him on Twitter, but also he has gotten started at ESPN Radio 97.5 as a producer in addition to doing some podcasts and some Substack work. We have Baltimore this week, but Baltimore was not interested in doing five questions, so I pivoted to family. Battle Red Blog: A lot has been made of the Texans underachieving their preseason expectations. What do you think are the biggest areas where they have fallen short and do you see it getting better in the last seven games? Jacob Barzilla: I would say the biggest issues have been the defensive regression and late-game execution. They are one of 10 teams in the NFL that are top 15 in EPA/Play on both offense and defense, but the only team that has fewer than 6 wins of that group. Unfortunately, the special teams group getting off to a horrific start didn’t help either. Kai Kroeger had a terrible Week 2 and cost the team points, and the team also struggled in short-yardage situations without Nico Collins. BRB: Even with recent victories there are those that want certain assistant coaches and/or executives let go. Which coaches do you think are on the hot seat and should they be? JB: I don’t think many coaches or executives are currently on the hot seat. Matt Burke is probably out after they stripped away his play-calling and I could see Rod Wright take that spot. Nick Caserio could also be on the hot seat, but I do think the roster is talented and he has drafted well, so I think they will likely give him another season no matter what. top.description: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes greets wife, Brittany Mahomes, during warmups prior to the game against the Washington Commanders at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. © Reuters Connect The Kansas City Chiefs’ Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Buffalo Bills went down to the wire. However, shortly before the game-winning field goal, a controversial call against Rashee Rice stopped what could’ve been a promising Chiefs drive with the score tied at 10-10. On a 3rd-and-10 play, Rice leaped to catch a contested ball; however, as he fell to the ground, the ball touched the turf, and after review, the referees ruled it an incomplete pass. top.title: Fury cleared to fight Anthony Joshua despite mental health concerns
top.description: FILE PHOTO - British boxer Tyson Fury celebrates his victory over Ukraine's Vladimir Klitschko after their world heavyweight title bout at the Esprit Arena in Duesseldorf. (is associated with: «Fury cleared to fight Anthony Joshua despite mental health concerns») Rolf Vennenbernd/dpa Tyson Fury has been cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month despite concerns about his mental health. The British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) indicated earlier this week that it would investigate comments from Fury’s wife Paris that the boxer had been diagnosed with schizophrenia, and had the powers to deny him a licence to fight. However, Paris Fury retracted her claim in a statement issued on Thursday night, and the BBBoC’s general secretary Robert Smith told Sky Sports: “Fury cleared last night. All up to date medicals cleared. Promoter told this morning.” Paris Fury said in an initial version of a Netflix documentary due for release today that Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after beating Wladimir Klitschko to win the world heavyweight title in Dusseldorf in November 2015. She said in Thursday’s statement: “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Netflix indicated it had edited the footage as a result, saying in a statement: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a near three-year hiatus from boxing, with his weight ballooning to 27 stone, while he battled suicidal thoughts and alcohol addiction. Fury admitted hearing “voices in my mind” following his win, adding: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.”

nigeria.title: Full list: African countries where travelers can access without visa
nigeria.description: Travelling across Africa is becoming easier as more countries adopt visa-free entry policies aimed at promoting tourism, strengthening regional integration and encouraging trade among African nations. Several African countries have introduced policies allowing citizens of other African countries to visit without obtaining a visa before travelling, reducing the cost and administrative hurdles associated with cross-border movement. Among the countries offering such access are Benin, The Gambia, Rwanda, Seychelles, Ghana and Togo. The policies form part of wider efforts to improve freedom of movement across the continent and advance the African Union’s goal of greater economic integration. The six countries are highlighted below, although their entry arrangements are not identical. 1. Benin Benin is one of Africa’s leading supporters of visa-free movement. It allows citizens of other African countries to enter without obtaining a visa before travelling. The country has promoted easier cross-border movement to encourage tourism, business and regional cooperation. 2. The Gambia The Gambia offers visa-free entry to citizens of other African countries. It is one of the continent’s more open destinations, making it attractive to visitors interested in tourism, business and cultural exchanges. 3. Rwanda Rwanda allows citizens of African Union member states to enter without a visa. The policy supports the country’s efforts to attract African visitors, investors and business travellers. 4. Seychelles Seychelles operates a visa-free entry policy for visitors of all nationalities, including African travellers. However, visitors must obtain the required travel authorisation before departure and meet the country’s entry conditions. 5. However, an application and approval are still required, meaning the policy is not strictly visa-free entry. 6. Togo Togo has introduced visa-free entry for African passport holders, subject to pre-arrival requirements. The policy is part of efforts to facilitate movement across the continent and strengthen regional integration. nigeria.title: Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim that boxer has schizophrenia
nigeria.description: Paris Fury, the wife of British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury, has withdrawn her earlier claim that her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying that he has never been formally diagnosed with the condition. Paris made the clarification after an earlier version of an upcoming Netflix documentary about the boxer featured her describing him as having “mild schizophrenia”. In a statement, she said she had used the term while recalling a conversation about Tyson’s mental health struggles several years ago, but acknowledged that it was not an accurate description of his medical history. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” she said. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” She added that mental health was complex and that finding the right words to describe someone’s experiences was not always easy. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love,” she said. Paris also praised her husband for speaking openly about his struggles and thanked the public for supporting their family. Netflix confirmed that it had updated the documentary following the family’s clarification about Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis. “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch,” the streaming platform said. The earlier comments had attracted attention from the British Boxing Board of Control, which indicated that it was investigating the matter. The 38 year old boxer is scheduled to face Joshua in an all British heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11, with the vacant WBA title expected to be at stake. Tyson has previously spoken publicly about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, when he became world heavyweight champion. After the victory, he took a break of nearly three years from boxing, during which he battled suicidal thoughts, drug and alcohol problems, and significant weight gain. Reflecting on that period in the documentary, Tyson said he experienced severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” he said. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” He later returned to boxing and regained the world heavyweight title by defeating Deontay Wilder in February 2020. nigeria.title: Arsenic In The Water: Thailand Presses Myanmar Over Mining Pollution
nigeria.description: As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation. Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits. Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group on the issue — also attended by the Chinese ambassador — where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were causing the pollution downstream. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This photo taken on June 5, 2026 shows Wan Wiriya, assistant professor from Chiang Mai University, showing the results of an arsenic level test from a water sample (C) taken from the Kok River, next to a control sample of drinking water (R) near the the northern Thai city of Chiang Rai. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP But there was no public agreement to Thailand’s request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar’s military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent. Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead. Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. “Now with the mines the fish are all gone,” she said. ‘Not from nature’ This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows fishermen and their boats near the confluence of the Kok River and Mekong River in Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP At the joint talks, Thai ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side. “Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar’s) Shan state, no-one disagrees,” Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue. Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. “This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity,” he told AFP. But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be “really difficult”, he added. nigeria.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
nigeria.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. The programme is part of Italy’s efforts to address labour shortages through regulated migration while strengthening cooperation with countries of origin. nigeria.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total. nigeria.title: Powerful Storm Disrupts US Thanksgiving, Leaves Over 900,000 Without Power
nigeria.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were cancelled, and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organisers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was cancelled for three years during World War II. Organisers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. Stay Safe People brave the bad weather in the Manhattan borough of New York City on November 26, 2026. Photo by KENA BETANCUR / AFP While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes. Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption. Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency Wednesday over the weather, urged residents to take precautions to stay safe. “Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines,” she wrote on X. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). sports.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images For Miami Dolphins edge rusher Josh Uche , the 2026 NFL season has been more than just another stop on a winding professional journey—it has been a long-awaited homecoming. Signed to a one-year contract in March after bouncing across three teams in two years, the 28-year-old Miami native has quietly re-emerged as a reliable, every-down contributor for a rebuilding Dolphins defense. Early Promise and Breakout in New England Drafted by the New England Patriots in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of the University of Michigan, Uche quickly earned a reputation as an explosive, twitchy pass-rush specialist. After battling injuries and adjusting to the pro game over his first two seasons, he exploded onto the scene in 2022. Operating alongside Matthew Judon, Uche racked up 11.5 sacks and two forced fumbles in 15 games, looking every bit like a cornerstone defender for New England’s future. Two Years of Uncertainty However, replicating that 2022 magic proved difficult. Following a three-sack 2023 campaign, Uche re-signed with New England on a short-term deal before being shipped to the Kansas City Chiefs at the 2024 trade deadline. In Kansas City, Uche struggled to crack Steve Spagnuolo’s defensive rotation, appearing in just six games without recording a sack. Seeking a fresh start in 2025, he signed with the Philadelphia Eagles . While he generated solid pressure rates in limited passing-down snaps, he finished the year with just one sack across 12 appearances, leaving his NFL trajectory at a crossroads entering free agency. Reviving His Career in South Florida When Miami brought Uche home in March 2026, the move flew largely under the radar. Initially viewed as a low-cost depth addition to a revamped linebacker room, Uche has outperformed expectations. Through the first 11 weeks of the 2026 season, Uche has already surpassed his combined sack total from the previous two campaigns: Defensive Production: 38 total tackles, 3.0 sacks, 24 total quarterback pressures, and one forced fumble. Expanded Role: Rather than being pigeonholed strictly as a third-down specialist, Uche has logged over 420 defensive snaps and earned strong marks for his run defense—proving he can hold the edge on early downs as well as collapse the pocket. Looking Ahead For a Dolphins squad navigating roster turnover and key injuries during the 2026 campaign, Uche’s steady play has been a bright spot. Returning to the AFC East—and getting the chance to square off against his former Patriots squad twice a year—has given the South Florida product a renewed edge. As Miami enters the final stretch of the season, Uche is making a compelling case that his best football is still ahead of him right in his own backyard. The Rossoneri overturned a two-goal deficit to claim a vital victory and keep their European hopes alive. Trailing 2-0 after Mike Maignan's own goal and a superb strike from Jota Silva, Milan looked destined for another damaging defeat. Hutchinson sparked the revival in the 56th minute, picking up possession near halfway, driving forward, cutting inside and firing calmly into the far corner. The winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser seven minutes later before creating the 71st-minute volley that saw substitute Christian Pulisic put Milan ahead. Diego Moreira sealed the 4-2 triumph in stoppage time on a counter-attack involving Pulisic. Amorim hands full credit to Hutchinson Following the final whistle, Amorim played down his own tactical adjustments and insisted Hutchinson's individual brilliance decided the contest. "I didn't change the game," the former Manchester United manager told reporters. "[Goncalo] Ramos came off because he was in pain, so it was a normal substitution. Hutchinson changed the game more than I did. What changed was the first goal." Amorim made it clear that such an influential display came as no surprise, while challenging the winger to maintain his high standards. "I always expect this from him," he added. sports.description: FILE PHOTO - British boxer Tyson Fury celebrates his victory over Ukraine's Vladimir Klitschko after their world heavyweight title bout at the Esprit Arena in Duesseldorf. (is associated with: «Fury cleared to fight Anthony Joshua despite mental health concerns») Rolf Vennenbernd/dpa Tyson Fury has been cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month despite concerns about his mental health. The British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) indicated earlier this week that it would investigate comments from Fury’s wife Paris that the boxer had been diagnosed with schizophrenia, and had the powers to deny him a licence to fight. However, Paris Fury retracted her claim in a statement issued on Thursday night, and the BBBoC’s general secretary Robert Smith told Sky Sports: “Fury cleared last night. All up to date medicals cleared. Promoter told this morning.” Paris Fury said in an initial version of a Netflix documentary due for release today that Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after beating Wladimir Klitschko to win the world heavyweight title in Dusseldorf in November 2015. She said in Thursday’s statement: “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Netflix indicated it had edited the footage as a result, saying in a statement: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a near three-year hiatus from boxing, with his weight ballooning to 27 stone, while he battled suicidal thoughts and alcohol addiction. Fury admitted hearing “voices in my mind” following his win, adding: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.”

technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

technology.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
technology.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. technology.title: British social security system techies yank services offline following 'cyber incident'
technology.description: The UK's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has taken some services offline after detecting a "cyber incident," but says regular benefit and pension payments are unaffected. The department announced the precautionary shutdown on Friday morning. "We have taken some DWP online services offline as a precaution after we identified a cyber incident affecting our systems," it said. "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre (GC3) to investigate and to bring services back online as quickly as possible and to minimize any disruption. "Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal. If an online service you need is unavailable, please try again later. As always, we will never message you to ask for bank details or ask you to click on links." The Register contacted both the DWP and NCSC for more information. The DWP declined to comment beyond the statement issued publicly. GC3 coordinates responses to incidents affecting government. The Government Cyber Unit leads the wider Government Cyber Action Plan, backed by more than £210 million. It is led by the government CISO, Bella Powell. Officials have not commented on any of the usual details one would expect from a cyber incident disclosure, including the specific services that were downed, when they are expected to return, or whether any data is thought to be compromised, even at this early stage. The UK government has also been criticized recently for investing heavily in AI cyber defenses, while the issue of legacy and aging IT continues to be neglected in the background. It announced at the end of October that it was throwing £130 million at AI cyber defense technology , as part of a wider £600 million cross-government AI spending spree announced by the Treasury. ExfilSquad recently claimed to have stolen around 607,000 records from the Department for Education and another 114,000 from the Police National Legal Database. ®

technology.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
technology.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

technology.title: Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids
technology.description: Volvo provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and accommodation so Ars could drive the XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015 , both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric . As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market . At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-new replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets. So instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base. Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also new, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Support team put in an emergency order for vodka – lots of vodka – to bring PCs back online
technology.description: The end of the working week is often enough to drive tech support people to drink, which is why The Register likes to get the party started early. Friday mornings bring a new installment of On Call – the column in which we share your stories of doing whatever it takes to keep tech running. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Bruce," who told us that in the mid-2000s he worked for a global radio station. "We used to have about 30 PCs, all running slightly different radio shows depending on the time zone where we broadcast," he explained. The PCs were old clunkers running Windows 95 long after Microsoft ended support for the OS. Management knew the machines needed replacing, but funding was probably another year away. "We had to coax them on till then," Bruce wrote. "And by coax, I mean we were buying RAM on eBay because nobody sold the 4MB sticks we needed anymore." Thanks to the tender ministrations of Bruce and his colleagues, the PCs kept humming and the radio stations stayed on the air. Until a lovely spring Tuesday, when Bruce and his crew enjoyed a bucolic cup of tea in the first real sunshine of the season and received a call informing them that one of the stations was down. One of Bruce's mates figured a cranky old PC probably just needed a reboot and headed off to fix it while the rest of the team enjoyed their tea. And then the phone rang again to report another outage, so Bruce and the entire crew went back to work, chatting about which switch or other shared device could have taken out two PCs. When they arrived in the office, the chap who had gone to reboot the first PC ran in and announced that the computer room had flooded. Bruce and his teammates ran into that room and found dirty brown water all over the floor, walls, ceiling, and the racks holding the ancient PCs. technology.title: AWS adds virtual iPhones to its cloud
technology.description: AWS now offers two new types of cloudy computers: emulated Androids and simulated iPhones. The cloudy colossus announced both virtual offerings on Wednesday. They’re part of its Device Farm service, which previously saw AWS offer developers the chance to test their software on actual iOS and Android devices that reside in the Amazonian cloud. AWS will now also host virtual devices running Android and iOS. AWS touts the virtual mobile devices as superior to physical devices. “With virtual devices, you can shift testing left to stages that need high speed and volume, such as pull requests, code merges, and smoke tests, and keep real devices for later stages that need high fidelity, such as regression and release testing,” the cloudy business unit argues in its launch announcement. AWS also says developers can get to work faster on a virtual iPhone or Pixel. “Virtual devices running the latest device and OS typically start in seconds, and others start in around a minute,” the outfit argues. That may sound appetizing, but Amazon’s menu of virtual devices is short and bland. When The Register logged on as an AWS user, the only emulated Android phone listed was a Google Pixel 10, running Android 15, 16, or 17. An emulated Pixel tablet running Android 17 is also on the menu. At the time of writing, we could find only a virtual iPhone 16, running iOS 18.6, 23.61, and 27.0. Analyst firm Counterpoint’s list of the world’s top 10 best-selling smartphones in Q2 of 2026 does not include a single Pixel device. The iPhone 16 occupies 10 th place. iPhone 17 models occupy the first, second, third, and seventh place on the list. AWS might excite more developers if it adds emulators for the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Galaxy A07 4G, A17 5G, A17 4G, and Galaxy S26, as they occupy the fourth, fifth, sixth, eighth and ninth places on Counterpoint’s list. Amazon’s choice of a Pixel tablet is also an oddity given analyst firm IDC doesn’t list Google among its top five tablet vendors . Amazon does offer physical Galaxy A17 devices and three versions of the iPhone 17. But Device Farm doesn’t offer any foldable devices, meaning developers struggling to wrap their heads around the iPhone Duo will need either ask Apple for a loaner or shell out $2,000 to acquire one. At least developers don’t have to change behavior to access the few virtual devices AWS offers, as existing Device Farm APIs and test frameworks will work on real or notional machines. ®

technology.title: Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug
technology.description: India’s free e-government platform has a critical SQL injection flaw that thousands of organizations must patch to protect up to two billion citizens. The platform is called the Digital Infrastructure for Governance (Impact and Transformation) – aka DIGIT – and is a modular suite that offers common services such as authentication and payment collection. Third party developers can also create DIGIT modules, and plenty have done so and now offer add-ons that handle tasks as diverse as managing birth and death certificates, revenue collection, and running water treatment plants. DIGIT is ubiquitous in India, where all state and union territory governments use the platform, as do over 20,000 local government entities. India also exports DIGIT under its policy of turning software created for its own needs into “digital public goods” (DPI) that it happily gives away to other nations. Nine nations have implemented DIGIT to some degree, among them Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Nigeria, Burundi, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Jamaica, and Sri Lanka India’s population is 1.4 billion. Indonesia’s is 280 million and Nigeria is home to 240 million. DIGIT is therefore used by governments that serve over two billion people, some of whom are now at risk thanks to CVE-2026-136706 , a 9.3-rated SQL injection flaw present in DIGIT which allows “improper neutralization of user supplied input while constructing SQL queries and execution in the affected User and Access Control Service components.” “An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted input through the affected API endpoint to the targeted system,” according to CERT-IN . “Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries, potentially resulting in unauthorized disclosure, modification or deletion of database information on the targeted system.” eGov India, which oversees work on DIGIT, has released source code for an update that fixes the problem. While local government users of DIGIT typically access it as SaaS, through large implementations run by national or state governments, over 1,000 deployments are live across various cities and other entities. Those orgs can therefore add patching DIGIT to their urgent to-do lists, along with fixing Java , PHP , vCenter and any other widely used technologies that suddenly need an urgent security update. ®

technology.title: The token factory never sleeps
technology.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. technology.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
technology.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses.
